heroLead: Meridian is one of those small Butler County communities where the mineral rights and the surface ownership have quietly gone their separate ways over the past couple generations.
intro: If you own minerals near Meridian, chances are the property traces back to a farm that's since been sold, subdivided, or passed down piecemeal to several family members. Butler County has plenty of that history, and it means figuring out exactly what fraction of a well you're entitled to can take some real digging.
We buy mineral and royalty interests around Meridian directly. We do the title work ourselves and explain what we find, rather than asking you to interpret an old deed on your own.

sections.heading: How a Farm Becomes a Fraction
paragraphs: A single Butler County farm from the early 1900s might have been split among four or five children, each of whom later passed their share to their own children. By the time a well gets drilled decades later, the original hundred-acre tract can be represented by a dozen small decimal interests, each one legitimate but easy to lose track of.
If your royalty check shows a decimal interest with several zeros after the point, that's often exactly what's happened, and it doesn't mean the interest isn't real or worth pursuing.

sections.heading: What Operators Are Doing Near Meridian
paragraphs: Butler County sits in the wet-gas portion of the Marcellus fairway, and operators have continued to develop pads through the county's townships over the past several years. Wells here typically show the steep early decline common to Marcellus horizontal wells before leveling into a longer, lower-volume production tail.
We look at where your interest sits relative to any active or recently completed units nearby, since that context matters as much as the well's own numbers.

sections.heading: Recorder of Deeds Research, Done For You
paragraphs: We pull your chain of title through the Butler County Recorder of Deeds so we understand exactly how your interest was created and confirm it's clear to transfer before we ever discuss a number.

faqs.question: My decimal interest looks tiny on the statement. Is it worth selling?
faqs.answer: Small decimals are common when a farm has been divided among many heirs over time. Even a small decimal tied to an active unit can carry real value, so it's worth a review.

faqs.question: Do you need my siblings or cousins to agree before you can buy my share?
faqs.answer: No. We can typically buy your individual interest on its own, regardless of what other co-owners decide to do with theirs.

faqs.question: What if I've lost my copy of the lease?
faqs.answer: We can usually locate lease and division order information through the operator once we know the well or unit your interest is tied to.
